title: ExCSV JSON profile
description: A JSON serialization of an ExCSV document. Carries the same vocabulary as the text form (#!excsv header, #@ metadata, #column schema, #% aggregates, #$ SQL) so the two round-trip losslessly. The CSV text form stays canonical; this profile is for JSON-native contexts (APIs, config, LLM structured output).

layout.description: Document shape. inline/sidecar are single-table (use root-level columns/data/reference); pack is multi-table (use tables[]).

csv.description: How to reconstruct the canonical CSV text form. All optional; omit to accept defaults. Purely a round-trip hint — it does not affect the JSON data.

header.description: Whether the canonical CSV carries a header row (column names come from `columns`).

null.description: Extra non-empty strings that also mean null in the CSV form. In JSON, null is the literal null.

meta.description: File-level metadata (#@ lines). Known keys below; any additional key is allowed.

grain.description: What one data row represents, e.g. 'one row per order'.

columns.description: Column schema (#column lines). Array order is the physical column order; a column's position is its index unless `index` is given explicitly.

aggregates.description: Pre-computed aggregates (#% lines). Each key is an aggregation name; each value is an array with one entry per physical column (null = not applicable / not computed). The array length should equal the number of physical columns.

ddl.description: Schema statements, executed in array order.

csvw.description: Optional embedded W3C CSVW metadata (arbitrary JSON object).

schema.description: Which schema wins when both `columns` and `csvw` are present.

checksum.description: Integrity fingerprint of the data, '<algorithm>:<hex-digest>'. Advisory.

rows.description: Number of data rows (excluding the header). For inline data this should equal data.length.

reference.description: Sidecar mode: relative path to an external CSV/TSV data file. Mutually exclusive with `data`.

data.description: Data rows as an array of arrays (one inner array per row, one cell per column, in `columns` order). No header row is embedded — names live in `columns`. Absent in sidecar or header-only stubs.

tables.description: Pack (multi-table) payload. One entry per table. When present, root-level columns/aggregates/sql/data/reference are not used — those live inside each table.

fk.description: Pack foreign keys — an informational relationship map (#fk lines). Not enforced.

not.description: A document cannot be both inline (data) and sidecar (reference).
A pack (tables) cannot also carry root-level inline data.
A pack (tables) cannot also carry a root-level sidecar reference.

cell.description: One CSV cell. JSON null is a true null. For decimal/long/int64, encode as string to avoid IEEE-754 precision loss; the column `type` tells consumers how to read it.

index.description: Zero-based position. Defaults to the array index.

unit.description: Unit of measurement, e.g. USD, kg, ms.

role.description: Analytical role, independent of storage type.

separator.description: Sub-field separator inside a single cell.

enum.description: Closed set of allowed non-null values (typed per `type`). In the text form this is a pipe-separated string; in JSON it is an array.

default.description: Schema/DDL default. Not applied when reading data.

statement.description: A single SQL statement, optionally tagged by dialect and version.

dialect.description: e.g. ansi, mysql, postgres, clickhouse. Omitted = ansi / header default.

stmt.description: The SQL statement (single statement, no embedded newlines needed).

table.description: One table inside a pack. Mirrors a single-table document, plus a name.

name.description: Table name. Unique within the pack.

meta.description: Table-level metadata (#@ lines in the table's _header).

fk.description: An informational foreign key: from <table>.<column> to <table>.<column>.
